newsitem.title: JAPAN: Pioneer expects 1997/98 group net profit Y8-9 bln.
newsitem.headline: Pioneer expects 1997/98 group net profit Y8-9 bln.

text.p: Pioneer Electronic Corp said on Monday that it expects to meet its group net profit forecast for fiscal 1997/98 of eight to nine billion yen, assuming an average dollar/yen rate for the year of 117 yen per dollar, as projected in the earnings forecast.

Pioneer executive vice president Masaaki Sono told a news conference that the company expects to produce 20 billion yen worth of laser disc products in 1997/98, down three billion yen from the prior year.

Pioneer on Monday announced its group results for the first quarter of fiscal 1997/98, which began on April 1. The company recorded a group pretax profit of 2.35 billion yen, up from 766 million yen in the year-ago period, and a group net profit of 1.03 billion yen versus 804 million yen.
"First quarter sales were aided by the yen's decline against the dollar, which raised group sales by 5.48 billion yen," Sono said.
He added that robust sales of car audio equipment in Europe, Southeast Asia and Latin America were a leading contributor to group profits.
He said that the ratio of Pioneer's overseas sales to total sales was 66.2 percent in the first quarter of 1997/98, up from 61.8 percent in the same period last year.
The company produces 48 percent of its goods overseas, and Sono said that is unlikely to change significantly in the near future.

In the April-June period, Pioneer's sales on the domestic market fell 11.0 percent from the same period a year ago but its sales abroad rose a year-on-year 7.8 percent, the company said in a statement.

Domestic sales dropped due to a fall in sales of laser disc products, on-line karaoke systems and car electronics products, although sales of laser-disc compatible DVD players, mini-disc compact stereo systems and telephones were strong, it said.
Sales of new car navigation systems with DVD-ROM drives, introduced in late June, were also robust, it said.
All of Pioneer's divisions, except for the audio equipment division and the audio and video software division, marked higher sales in the 1997/98 first quarter.
In the April-June period, sales at Pioneer's audio equipment division fell 3.9 percent year-on-year, while the software division recorded a 42.1 percent drop.
"Unlike last year, we did not have any hit CDs in the first quarter of this business year," the statement said.
Pioneer said that its restructuring efforts in Japan during the prior business year also contributed to growth in its first-quarter group profit.
